## Summary

Fixed the layout bug and widened the modal in `NewEpicCard.tsx`:

**Root cause of the overlap/off-ness**: the front/back faces toggled between `position: static` and `position: absolute` depending on `advanced`. Since only one face was ever "in flow" at a time, the container's height was driven by whichever face happened to be static — the instant you clicked the toggle, the layout height snapped to the *other* face's height before the 3D rotation even started animating, so the visible face got stretched/cropped against a height that belonged to the face flipping in. That read as overlapping/jumbled content mid-flip.

**Fix**: both faces are now permanently `position: absolute; inset: 0` inside a perspective box with a real fixed height (`min(760px, 84vh)`) — never toggled, so there's nothing to snap. Each face is a `flex flex-col` with its own header, a scrollable body (`flex-1 overflow-y-auto`), and a footer pinned to the bottom with a `border-t` divider — so long content (a big Agent Library, a wide grounding board) scrolls internally instead of stretching or clipping the card.

**Wider modal**: max-width went from a fixed 660px/860px to `min(920px, 92vw)` (front) / `min(1320px, 94vw)` (advanced/grounding board) — it now uses most of the available page width on typical windows instead of a narrow fixed column, while still capping sanely on very wide displays.

The Project Home is not getting build from the Components Lirbrary work, this means that some of the final wiring is not there; We want to fill in the components from the library and arrange a home page as part of the generate action on the home page. Committed. The remaining modified files (agentLibrary.cjs, AgentLibrary.tsx, etc.) belong to other concurrent Epics running against this same repo — not part of this task, left untouched.

## Diagnosis

**Root cause**: the entire Project Pages pipeline (Stage 0 renderer, Stage 1 summary schema, Stage 2 selection scorer, Stage 3 render, Stage 4 UI in `ProjectPagesSection.tsx`) was already fully built and correctly wired — but had **never actually been run** for this project. `session-manager-operations/project-pages/` only had a `README.md`; no `summary.json`, `picks.json`, or `output/*.html` existed, so Project Home was permanently stuck on the "No Project Pages yet" empty state. That reads as "not getting built from the Components Library work," but the wiring itself checked out clean end-to-end.

## Fix

Ran the actual generate pipeline for session-manager itself, following `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`'s protocol:
1. Composed `summary.json` from real, traceable facts only (`brief.json`, CLAUDE.md, git log, file/test counts) — no fabricated stats or testimonials (`quotes: []`).
2. Validated it (`validate-project-pages-summary.cjs` → `valid`).
3. Ran the Stage 2 selection scorer → `picks.json`.
4. Built and ran the Stage 0 renderer → `output/{marketing,feature,architecture}.html` + `manifest.json`.
5. Confirmed no `undefined` leaked into the generated HTML, all 30 existing `projectPages`/`ProjectHome` unit tests pass, and `npm run typecheck` is clean.

Committed the artifacts (`2224fdc`) so Project Home's iframe now has real content instead of the empty state. The "Regenerate" button will re-run this same chain from the app once a `project-home-builder` Epic session does it interactively.

## Answers

**What is the Agent called?** `project-home-builder`.

**Was it registered in the Agent Library?** No — that was the actual gap. `AgentLibrary.tsx`/`agentLibrary.cjs` only enumerate global personas at `~/.claude/agents/*.md`, and this agent's definition lived *only* at this repo's `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`. Worse: `.gitignore`'s `.claude/agents/*` rule whitelisted `builder.md` but never `project-home-builder.md` — so it was silently untracked the whole time, invisible both to Agent Library and to git. Fixed both:
- Added `!.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` to `.gitignore` and committed the file.
- Added the missing global counterpart `~/.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md` (generic protocol shape), so this repo's project file now overlays it — same "global generic + project overlay" convention `builder.md` already uses. It now shows up in Agent Library like any other persona.

**What tag gets assigned?** Epic tag `project-home-builder` (the Mission/"what" axis, `tagLibrary.ts`/`agentTagDefs.ts`) — deliberately excluded from `AGENT_TAG_ORDER` so it can't be hand-picked in the New Epic composer; it's only ever assigned by the Generate Now/Regenerate buttons.

**On your actual ask** ("Generate should kick off an Agent with dedicated grounding: review templates → select → generate content → build+host, via Epics/session-manager-operations"): that flow was already the design (`agentTagDefs.ts`'s `initialPromptTemplate` grounds the session to read the pipeline spec + component library README, follow `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`'s protocol, then write `summary.json`→`picks.json`→`output/*.html`, which Project Home hosts in a sandboxed iframe). The missing piece was that the Epic had a mission (tag) but no bound *identity* (agentType) — now fixed: `ProjectPagesSection.tsx` resolves the registered persona via `listPersonas()` and passes it into `composeEpicIntake`/`createPromptSession` exactly like `NewEpicCard.tsx` does for a …

Pushed to `origin/main` (`f1c01af..cf752fe`), including this Epic's commits: `2224fdc` (ran the Project Pages generate pipeline) and `67c2326` (registered `project-home-builder` in the Agent Library + wired Generate Now to it).

Left untouched: several other files still modified/uncommitted in the working tree (`agentLibrary.cjs`, `AgentLibrary.tsx`, `TagLibrary.tsx`, etc.) — those belong to other concurrent Epics running against this same repo, not this one.

## Diagnosis

**Root cause**: `chat.ts`'s `onComplete`/`onNeedsInput` handlers (`src/renderer/state/chat.ts:910-912, 917-918`) do two things on every completed assistant turn:
1. `pushTurn(...)` — appends the reply as a live `ChatTurn`, rendered in `EpicDetail`'s Discussion timeline via the fully-formatted `<Turn>` bubble.
2. `appendResponseEvent(tabId, finalMessage)` — appends a `'response'`-kind `PromptSessionEvent` with the *same text*, whose real purpose (per `promptSessions.ts`'s `mergeAppendedEvent`) is to toast the user when a **different, unfocused** Epic gets an update.

`EpicDetail.tsx`'s merged `timeline` (lines 377-384, pre-fix) rendered **every** `'response'` event regardless of whether the Epic was currently focused, via the compact `<ResponseEvent>` component — so the same assistant message showed up twice: once as the normal chat bubble, once as a second, unstyled/compact line right below it. That second line is what read as "raw" to you — same content, no bubble chrome, no tool trace.

This wasn't a problem for the events' *other* legitimate producers (scheduler PRD-completion notices via `notifyOriginatingTab`, Terminal-handoff markers) since those have no matching live `Turn` to duplicate — they're the intended "compact by default, expand for raw" pattern (`ResponseEvent`'s existing "show more" toggle).

## Fix

`src/renderer/components/epics/EpicDetail.tsx`: before merging `'response'` events into the timeline, filter out any whose text matches (or is a truncated prefix of) an already-rendered assistant `Turn`'s text. Genuinely out-of-band `'response'` events (no matching live turn) still render with their existing expand-on-demand summary.

Added a regression test in `EpicDetail.test.tsx` asserting a duplicated `'response'` event is suppressed while a distinct one (a PRD-finished notice) still renders. `tsc --noEmit` and the full `epics`/`chat`/`promptSessions` test suites (209 tests) pass.

That screenshot is a live example of the exact bug I just diagnosed and fixed in `EpicDetail.tsx`. You can see it clearly:

- **Top block** (with ✓ checkmarks, bold headers, code chips) — the properly formatted assistant `Turn` bubble rendering the "Summary" reply from a completed Epic turn.
- **Bottom block** (dense bold run-on text, no line breaks, no formatting) — the *same* summary text rendered a second time as a duplicate `'response'` PromptSessionEvent via `ResponseEvent`'s `[&_*]:inline [&_*]:m-0` CSS override, which forces every markdown element (headers, lists, bold) onto one squashed inline line. For a short PRD-notice string that override just looks like a compact "— text —" line; for this much markdown content it collapses into the garbled bold wall of text you're seeing — which reads exactly like "the raw version" of the message.

This confirms the root cause precisely: `chat.ts`'s `onComplete` handler both `pushTurn`s the real formatted reply *and* `appendResponseEvent`s the identical text as an audit/toast event, and `EpicDetail.tsx` was rendering both. The fix already applied (this session, prior turn) filters `'response'` events out of the Discussion timeline when their text duplicates an already-rendered assistant `Turn`, while still showing genuinely out-of-band ones (PRD-completion notices with no matching live turn) via the same compact/expandable summary.

No further action needed on my end — the screenshot is corroborating evidence for the already-committed fix, not a new issue.
